use.flag:
Auto resolves firmware and kernel version required for full mitigation.
If enabled, this will remove LTS support.
If disabled, this will allow for LTS support if the microarchitecture mitigations are provided for that series or if the microarchitecture is not vulnerable.
Enabled is recommended for Intel® CPUs since the USE flag coverage for microarchitectures is incomplete.

Reject kernel package sources or prebuilt kernels that are behind in security updates or unable to disable unused ciphers.
Reject non-essential kernel modules required for data security or enterprise auditing.
Protect against data tampering by replacing vulnerable versions.
Use firmware as mitigation. (A BIOS firmware update from the motherboard manufacturer may still be required if the firmware package doesn't apply to your model.)
Check for data tampering mitigations for KVM.
Allow only landlock compatible kernels (5.13+) to mitigate path traversal, arbitrary file read, arbitrary file write.

Allow only kernels (6.10+) with mseal syscall support to mark virtual memory address immutable against permissions tampering, code injection, control-flow hijack.
Benefits:
Chromium: Mitigate RCE, code injection, CFI bypass, JIT spray glibc: Mitigate dynamic linker hijack
Mitigate against data tampering, privilege escalation, Spectre V1, Spectre V2 for the NVIDIA® video driver.
